findings: The official monthly series records a 12 per cent reduction in regional road deaths between the year to May 2022 and the year to November 2025, not 40 per cent. No published series supports a 40 per cent figure over any comparable period.
context: The comparison uses 12-month rolling totals to remove seasonal effects. Individual months vary widely. An updated release in September 2026 puts the reduction at 13 per cent; the classification is unchanged.

findings: The national accounts show real household disposable income per capita fell 4.6 per cent between the June quarter 2022 and the December quarter 2025. Nominal household disposable income rose 11 per cent over the same period. Neither series shows an 8 per cent fall.
context: 'Household disposable income' can be measured in nominal or real terms, in aggregate or per person. The per-capita real measure fell; the aggregate nominal measure rose. Mr Oyelaran subsequently corrected the figure to 'around 5 per cent in real per-capita terms'.

findings: This is a general evaluative statement. Whether Australians are 'worse off' depends on the measure chosen (real wages, disposable income, wealth, wellbeing surveys) and the comparison period. PUBLIC RECORD logs the statement for context and does not assess it.
context: Where a politician attaches a specific figure to a statement like this, the figure is recorded and checked as a separate claim.

findings: Program reporting records 40,300 dwellings approved for funding by 31 March 2026, of which 17,900 were completed. The 40,000 figure is accurate for approvals but not for completed homes.
context: 'Delivered' is ambiguous. Program documents distinguish approvals, commencements and completions. On 6 May 2026 Senator Natarajan restated the figure as 40,000 approved and around 18,000 complete.

findings: The market operator's quarterly report shows the volume-weighted average spot price for the March quarter 2026 was 18.4 per cent higher than in the March quarter 2025.
context: Wholesale prices are one component of retail bills; the claim was specifically about wholesale prices.

findings: The only published analysis is a cost-benefit summary commissioned by the port's proponent, which reports a benefit-cost ratio of 3.1 but does not publish its assumptions. No independent evaluation has been located.
context: A single proponent-commissioned source is below the evidence standard for a contested economic claim. The record will be updated if an independent evaluation is published.

findings: Departmental program data lists 1,940 kilometres of funded regional road upgrades, of which 1,120 kilometres were complete at February 2026. The figure is close for funded works; completed works are lower.
context: The claim referred to funded upgrades, which the data broadly supports. It would be contradicted if read as completed works.

findings: The initial June quarter 2026 rental price index showed annual growth of 5.1 per cent, higher than the 4.8 per cent recorded in 2021. On that release, the past year was not the slowest since 2020.
context: Superseded on 12 September 2026 after the series was revised.

findings: The September 2026 revision of the rental price index revised June quarter annual growth to 4.6 per cent nationally, below 2021. On the revised series the claim holds for the capital-city index (4.4 per cent) but not for the regional index (5.3 per cent).
context: Classification changed from 'Contradicted by evidence' to 'Mixed / context required' after revised data became available. The earlier assessment remains on the record.

findings: The statement describes a private conversation. The regulator has said it does not comment on private discussions. No record exists against which the claim can be tested.
context: Unverifiable claims are recorded so that later evidence can be attached, but they are not counted as supported or contradicted.

findings: This repeats a claim first checked on 9 January 2026. The updated August 2026 release of the official series records a 13 per cent reduction in regional road deaths over the comparable period, not 40 per cent.
context: The evidence was refreshed with the August 2026 release before this repetition was assessed. The result is unchanged.

findings: Taxation statistics for 2023–24 show Tasmania recorded the lowest median taxable income of any state or territory.
context: Median taxable income excludes people who do not lodge returns and is not the same as median household income.

findings: The national inventory records that emissions fell 1.2 per cent in 2023 and 0.8 per cent in 2024, and rose 0.4 per cent in 2025. Emissions did not rise in every year since 2022.
context: Annual inventory figures are revised over time. The claim was repeated unchanged on 12 August 2026.

findings: This is a prediction about future growth. It cannot be assessed against current evidence. It is logged so that it can be revisited if relevant data becomes available.

Net overseas migration peaked at 536,000 in 2022–23. The latest annual figure, 335,000 in 2024–25, is below that peak but well above the pre-2020 average. The cumulative three-year total is the highest on record.
context: 'Record levels' is accurate for the three-year cumulative total and inaccurate for the latest annual figure. Mr Oyelaran clarified on 29 September 2026 that he was referring to the cumulative total.

findings: Departmental Medicare statistics record a GP bulk-billing rate of 79.0 per cent for the June quarter 2026.
context: The bulk-billing rate counts services, not patients; the share of patients who are always bulk-billed is lower.

findings: The 2025 national assessment report puts 33.1 per cent of Tasmanian Year 9 students in the two lowest reading proficiency bands ('needs additional support' and 'developing'). Only 12.4 per cent are in the lowest band. The figure matches one reading of the data but not another, and applies to Year 9 rather than all students.
context: The assessment program replaced the old 'national minimum standard' with proficiency bands in 2023, so there is no longer a single 'minimum standard' figure.

findings: Budget Paper No. 1 for 2026–27 projects defence funding at 2.3 per cent of GDP in 2028–29.
context: Projections depend on GDP forecasts and are revised at each budget update.

findings: State recorded-crime statistics show burglary offences in the Wattle Plains local area rose 23 per cent over the two years to June 2026. They did not double.
context: Mr Oyelaran clarified on 3 August 2026 that he 'should have said break-ins have risen sharply, not doubled'.

findings: The latest published hospital resources data covers 2024–25 and shows Silvergum Hospital with 412 beds, 64 fewer than in 2020–21. No published data covers 2025–26, so the claimed 200-bed reduction cannot be tested for the full period.
context: PUBLIC RECORD has requested current bed numbers from the hospital network. The record will be updated when a response is received.
